title: Swierkiewicz v. Sorema N.A. (2002)
summary: The plaintiff did not have to plead every element of an evidentiary prima facie case of employment discrimination.
notes: Twombly and Iqbal later govern general plausibility. This decision remains important to the distinction between plausible factual allegations and prematurely demanding a complete trial proof structure.

sections.Parties: Swierkiewicz, an older employee of Hungarian national origin, sued Sorema for age and national-origin discrimination.
sections.Material Facts: The complaint described his position and experience, changes in responsibilities, replacement by a younger French employee with substantially less relevant experience, exclusion from business decisions, and the circumstances preceding his discharge. Those factual allegations identified the employment decisions and the basis for his claim of discriminatory treatment.
sections.Procedural History: The district court dismissed the complaint for failing to allege a prima facie case under the employment-discrimination burden-shifting framework. The Second Circuit affirmed. The Supreme Court reversed.
sections.Issue: Must an employment-discrimination complaint contain the facts needed to establish the McDonnell Douglas evidentiary prima facie case?
sections.Holding: No. That evidentiary framework did not create an additional heightened pleading requirement. The complaint met Rule 8.
sections.Reasoning: The method of proving discrimination may depend on evidence that is not yet available at filing. Direct evidence may make the burden-shifting framework unnecessary, and discovery may change the available route of proof. The Court therefore separated a trial evidentiary structure from the complaint’s notice function. The specific allegations about positions, personnel changes, and termination made the dispute intelligible. The Court also emphasized the Rules’ express treatment of situations requiring particularity rather than judicial addition of special requirements.

learning.why: The plaintiff did not have to plead every element of an evidentiary prima facie case of employment discrimination.

topics.cp-notice-pleading: A complaint can give fair notice through the employment chronology and alleged discriminatory treatment.
topics.cp-pleading-proof: The evidentiary framework for proving discrimination is not automatically a required pleading checklist.

mnemonic.rationale: A vice president demoted at fifty-three
